findings.title: Saved shutdown_drain_timeout is never used — scheduler still reads the import-time env constant
findings.problem: save_settings now parses and persists general.shutdown_drain_timeout, and settings_page renders it, but the only consumer of the drain timeout is triggarr/search/scheduler.py, which computes a module-level constant at import: `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT: float = _read_shutdown_drain_timeout()` (line 81) reading ONLY os.environ['TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT']. The shutdown path (lines 611, 618, 634 — `async with asyncio.timeout(_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT)`) uses that constant and never touches `settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout`. Grep across triggarr/ shows zero reads of the config field outside routes.py's own write and render. The setting therefore round-trips to TOML and displays correctly while having no effect on behavior — the documented precedence (config = default, env = override) is inverted to env-only.
findings.fix_hint: make the drain read settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout at shutdown time (pass it into _read_shutdown_drain_timeout as the default, applying the env override on top) instead of the import-time module constant
findings.why_it_matters: An operator changes the drain timeout in the UI, sees it saved and re-rendered, and the shutdown drain still waits the old 60s — in-flight search cycles are cut short (or the container is SIGKILLed) contrary to the configured value, with no error to indicate the setting was ignored.

findings.title: settings_page passes shutdown_drain_timeout but the template has no matching input, so every save resets it to 60.0
findings.problem: The context key is added at line 446 but triggarr/templates/settings.html contains no `name="shutdown_drain_timeout"` input (grep returns nothing; the General section stops at max_consecutive_failures/skip_unreleased). Consequently form.get("shutdown_drain_timeout") is always None on POST /settings, and safe_float returns its `default` of 60.0 — unlike neighboring preserved fields such as tracking_delay_seconds, which is read from current_settings.general. Any user who saves settings for an unrelated reason silently overwrites a configured drain timeout (e.g. 120.5 set via TOML) back to 60.0. This is the half-migration pattern: route + model landed, template did not. It also makes the already-committed test at tests/test_web.py:694 fail.
findings.fix_hint: add the number input (step allowing fractions, min 1, max 3600) to the General section of triggarr/templates/settings.html; until then fall back to current_settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout rather than the literal 60.0 in save_settings
findings.why_it_matters: A silent data-loss path: unrelated settings saves clobber a deliberately configured shutdown drain, and the feature is unreachable from the UI it was built for.

findings.title: Half-migrated config knob: routes.py adds the GET render var and POST parse but the settings.html form input is absent
findings.problem: Half-migrated config knob: the diff adds BOTH ends of the settings round-trip in routes.py (GET render var at routes.py:446, POST safe_float parse at routes.py:550) but the middle — the form input in triggarr/templates/settings.html — is absent. Verified by grep: settings.html contains inputs for tracking_window_minutes (line 67) and max_consecutive_failures (line 74) but ZERO occurrences of shutdown_drain_timeout. Consequences, both concrete: (1) the GET render var 'shutdown_drain_timeout' is dead — no template consumes it; (2) the POST parse permanently reads form.get('shutdown_drain_timeout') == None on every real browser submit, so safe_float returns its 60.0 default and RE-WRITES 60.0 over any operator's configured value on every unrelated settings save (e.g. someone changing log level silently resets a 120.5s drain to 60.0). This is a data-clobbering regression, not merely a missing UI. The phase's own plan 75-02-PLAN.md names settings.html as a required artifact ('provides: numeric drain-timeout input + precedence help text', 'contains: shutdown_drain_timeout') and declares key_link 'from: triggarr/templates/settings.html, to: {{ shutdown_drain_timeout }}, via: GET render dict in routes.py' — that link is unsatisfied by this diff. Test tests/test_web.py:694 asserts "shutdown_drain_timeout" in response.text and will FAIL against this diff.
findings.fix_hint: Add the numeric input to settings.html's General section alongside max_consecutive_failures, following that block's markup: type="number" name="shutdown_drain_timeout" value="{{ shutdown_drain_timeout }}" with a fractional step (0.1 or any), min="1" max="3600", plus the D-10 env-override precedence help text. Until the input exists, have the POST handler preserve current_settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout when the form key is absent (the pattern used at routes.py:548 for tracking_delay_seconds).

findings.title: Configured shutdown_drain_timeout is written to config but never consumed — scheduler still uses import-time module constant
findings.problem: The saved `general.shutdown_drain_timeout` value has no consumer. `triggarr/search/scheduler.py:81` binds `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT: float = _read_shutdown_drain_timeout()` ONCE at module import, and `_read_shutdown_drain_timeout()` (scheduler.py:58-74) reads only the `TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` env var with a hardcoded "60.0" default — it takes no `Settings` argument and never touches `app.state.settings`. All five shutdown-path uses (scheduler.py:611, 618, 634, 648, 656) read that module constant. So a user who sets the drain timeout to 120.5 in the UI sees it persist in triggarr.toml and round-trip in the form, but the actual shutdown drain still waits 60s. This is a genuine deferred split — 75-03-PLAN.md D-04/D-05 explicitly own the scheduler refactor — so this is intended-incomplete rather than a wrong-code defect. It is recorded because it is the ship-gating blast-radius fact: shipping 75-02 alone yields a settings control that visibly persists a value with zero runtime effect.
findings.current_code:
scheduler.py:81  _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT: float = _read_shutdown_drain_timeout()
scheduler.py:634  async with asyncio.timeout(_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT):
findings.fix_hint: No change in this diff — 75-03 (D-04/D-05) converts _read_shutdown_drain_timeout to take the configured value and resolves it locally in the shutdown block. Do not ship the UI input to users before 75-03 lands, or gate it.
findings.why_it_matters: A settings knob that persists but does nothing is worse than an absent one — operators will set it, verify it saved, and still get SIGKILLed mid-cycle at the 60s default during a Docker stop.

findings.title: Connect the saved timeout to the shutdown drain
findings.problem: POSTing 120.5 persists that value, but scheduler.py:634 still uses _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT, initialized exclusively from the environment or 60.0. Even after restart, the saved value is ignored. Operators attempting to extend the drain will still have resources forcibly closed after the old timeout.
findings.fix_hint: Resolve the timeout from the current app.state.settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout during shutdown, with an explicitly validated environment override, and test that a saved value controls the drain.
findings.why_it_matters: Operators attempting to extend the drain will still have resources forcibly closed after the old timeout.
